details:
Summary

Desktop users need the mouse wheel to adjust held object distance (Z-axis) as it worked in the legacy system. Third-person camera zoom should not override this essential object manipulation feature.

Current Behavior:

- In the current desktop implementation, mouse wheel scroll is locked to third-person camera zoom.

- When holding an object (pen, prop, etc.), scrolling the wheel no longer moves the object forward/backward along the Z-axis.

Legacy Behavior (Expected):

- When holding an object, mouse wheel scroll should adjust the object's distance from the user (Z-axis translation).

- This was the original behavior before the third-person view update and was critical for precise object placement.

Why This Matters:

- Object distance adjustment is used constantly: drawing, photography, prop placement, and world interaction all require fine Z-axis control.

- Third-person camera zoom is rarely needed: many desktop users don't use third-person view, or only toggle it occasionally for screenshots.

- The current design prioritizes an infrequent feature over a daily workflow tool, significantly reducing desktop usability.

Suggested Solutions:

1. Restore legacy behavior: When holding an object, scrollwheel adjusts object distance (Z-axis). When not holding anything, scrollwheel adjusts third-person camera (if enabled).

2. Context-sensitive priority: Object manipulation takes priority over camera controls when an object is in hand.

3. Optional toggle: Add a setting in Graphics or Controls to choose between "legacy object scroll" and "camera zoom priority."

Platform:

- Desktop (Windows)

- Input: Keyboard + Mouse

Tags: desktop, controls, third-person, accessibility, quality-of-life, input, legacy-behavior
title: Restore legacy scrollwheel behavior for object distance adjustment on desktop
